quotes.text: You need a way to ingest massive amounts of data, buffer it so you don't lose anything, and distribute it to multiple consumers all in real time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the streaming problem that Event Hubs is built to solve.

quotes.text: A database stores data so you can query it later. But a stream is different. It's a continuous flow of events that multiple readers can read independently at their own pace without removing anything from the stream.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates streams from queues and databases.

quotes.text: The key insight is that event hubs completely decouples producers from consumers. Producers don't know who's reading their data. Consumers don't know who's sending the data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the architectural benefit of decoupling.

quotes.text: Event hubs is the security camera. It records everything for playback and analysis. It's built for high volume streaming, millions of events per second, and multiple consumers can read the same stream independently.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy that sets Event Hubs apart from Event Grid and Service Bus.

quotes.text: The key takeaway is this, event hubs is the pipe, not the processing engine. It ingests and distributes data, pair it with functions, stream analytics, or data bricks for the real value.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets realistic expectations about what Event Hubs does on its own.

chapters.title: Event Hubs vs. Event Grid vs. Service Bus
Getting started with a simple architecture

takeaways: Azure Event Hubs is a managed streaming platform, not a queue or database, that ingests millions of events per second and lets multiple consumer groups read the same stream independently.
Partitions preserve order and enable parallelism, throughput units define capacity, and retention plus checkpointing allow consumers to replay and resume reliably.

Use Event Grid to react to changes, Service Bus for guaranteed transactional messaging and Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry, paired with a processing engine such as Azure Functions or Stream Analytics.
hook: Nightly batch jobs and traditional queues break down when thousands of sensors or services send data every second. This episode explains Azure Event Hubs in plain English for developers and architects building real-time pipelines. You learn how partitions, consumer groups and throughput units work and when to choose Event Hubs over Event Grid or Service Bus.
